title: Speculative recall prefetch during long tool calls (instrument + flag-gated prototype)
description:
## Context

Long tool calls (`cargo test`, builds, dependency downloads) leave a multi-second idle window where the main model waits. MC computes recall on the turn path today. This task hides recall latency and widens recall quality by pre-warming retrieval during that window, using the tool call itself as the query seed.

Origin: accepted item #1 from the 2026-08-22 speculative-execution brainstorm review. The wider proposal (advisory LLM branches, EV scheduler, speculative tool execution, KV transfer) was **rejected**; this task is deliberately the deterministic-retrieval-only slice. Do not scope-creep toward LLM speculation.

## Current State

- Recall/injection happens per turn: `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/inject-compartments.ts` (utility-tier assignment ~line 238), budgeted by `DEFAULT_MEMORY_BUDGET_TOKENS` (4k twin in `crates/mc-module/src/config.rs:22` and `packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts`).
- Tool boundary hooks already exist: `createToolExecuteAfterHook` at `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/hook-handlers.ts:510`; `tool.execute.before/after` handled across `hook.ts`, `transform.ts`.
- No tool-latency instrumentation exists (no prefetch/speculative code found; `bd search` negative).
- `magic-context-9o6.3` plans a *pre-action* deterministic classifier on the same hook surface (warn-only interrupts). Different purpose (safety warnings vs latency hiding), shared plumbing.

## Desired State

Measure-first, flag-gated prototype. Two deliverables:

1. **Tool-latency instrumentation** (always on, cheap): record per-tool-signature wall time (tool name + coarse args class) into the session DB. Output: observed latency distribution so the prefetch threshold is data-backed, and so 9o6.3 can reuse it.
2. **Prefetch path** (config flag, default off):
   - On `tool.execute.before`, if the tool signature's expected duration exceeds a single threshold constant (start: 5s; no EV scheduler, no resource-class model), fire the existing recall/search path asynchronously with queries derived from tool args + active task context.
   - Hold results in a session-scoped buffer keyed by `(sessionId, callID)`, hard-capped (e.g. 4 entries, drop oldest). `ponytail:` fixed cap + drop-oldest; smarter eviction only if measurement demands it.
   - On `tool.execute.after` / next transform, deliver only fragments that pass the *existing* injection tiering and token budget. Unused entries dropped at turn end. Zero prompt change when flag off.
   - If retrieval hasn't completed by delivery time, skip silently (same discipline as 9o6.3).
3. **Metrics**: prefetch hit rate (prefetched fragment actually injected), recall latency saved on the turn path, wasted-work rate. Kill criterion: hit rate or latency savings too low → delete the flag and keep only the instrumentation.

**Simplicity gate:** reuse the existing recall entry points (`ctx_search` internals / injection pipeline); no new retrieval engine, no advisory types, no observation predicates. The only new mechanism is the trigger + bounded holding buffer.

## Implementation Guidance

### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/hook-handlers.ts` | latency capture at tool boundary; prefetch trigger | hooks already live here |
| `packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/inject-compartments.ts` | accept pre-warmed results at delivery | reuse existing tiering/budget |
| `packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts` | flag + threshold | config twin discipline |
| session storage (`storage-db.ts` or session_meta) | latency rows | instrumentation |

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check ran on "tool-hook-triggered background retrieval with held results" — outcome: **place-adjacent**. `9o6.3` (planned, not implemented) is the only sibling; no existing prefetch/holding code. Implementing agent must coordinate trigger plumbing so 9o6.3 and this share one tool-signature classifier when both land.

### Blast Radius
Hook path latency is user-visible: the `tool.execute.before` work must be fire-and-forget (async task), never awaited on the hook path. Buffer lives in memory per session; bounded.

## Design Notes
Productionizing beyond the flag-gated prototype (buffer sizing under concurrency, cross-provider behavior, query-derivation quality) goes through `/plan-forge` with the measurement data from deliverable 1. This task intentionally stops at instrumented prototype + metrics. (design-risk gate: mechanism kept to bounded buffer + single threshold; envelope check deferred to plan-forge with real data.)

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| magic-context-9o6.3 | JIT memory interrupts on tool hooks | relates-to (shared trigger surface, different purpose) |
| magic-context-3q5.5 | Stage-decomposed benchmark harness | relates-to (measurement rides it) |
| magic-context-9o6 | Action-triggered memory epic | relates-to (same "action as trigger" thesis) |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Per-tool-signature latency distribution recorded and queryable per session.
- [ ] Flag off ⇒ byte-identical prompt output (cache-parity baseline script unchanged).
- [ ] Flag on ⇒ no added blocking latency on the hook path (fire-and-forget verified).
- [ ] Delivered fragments pass existing injection budget/tiering; no new injection surface.
- [ ] Holding buffer hard-capped; entries dropped at turn end.
- [ ] Hit-rate / latency-saved / wasted-work metrics emitted.
- [ ] No new retrieval helper duplicating existing recall entry points.
- [ ] `cargo fmt && cargo check && cargo clippy` clean; bun tests pass.

## Pointers
- Brainstorm review (this session, 2026-08-22): rejected wider runtime; scope fence.
- `docs/perf/mc-host-baseline.md` for perf measurement conventions.
- 9o6.3 description for the skip-silently/hard-budget discipline to mirror.

title: Applicability engine + retrieval-time read repair
description:
Feedback-adoption (2026-08 design review). Runtime half of U6c's applicability/anchor schema (magic-context-3q5.32). Recreated after dedup against main (was local U33/3q5.34).

## Goal
At retrieval time each candidate claim resolves to an applicability state against the caller's repo state; only `current` auto-injects; failed cheap checks repair the store instead of silently returning stale memory.

## Engine
- Reachability: is introduced_by/invalidated_by anchor reachable from current HEAD (git merge-base --is-ancestor; patch-id fallback for rebase/cherry-pick; tree/symbol-hash fallback when commits are gone).
- Dirty-tree overlap: uncommitted paths intersect affected_paths -> dirty_tree_uncertain.
- Cheap validity checks (read repair): referenced file exists, symbol still resolves, config key still present. Bounded per-query budget; results cached per (anchor, HEAD, dirty-fingerprint) generation — indexed point lookups in the spirit of R6, no per-candidate git subprocess spawns.
- On failure: mark stale/uncertain, append a verification_event (invalidation), schedule dreamer deep verification; never silently inject. Historical/uncertain stay reachable via explicit search, labeled.

## Interlocks
- Applicability is a hard lane filter beside trust (KTD19) for auto-inject; explicit search may include labeled historical results.
- Dreamer verify/map-memories remains the deep/batch layer; this unit is the cheap synchronous layer.
- Complements contradiction-first evidence bundles (magic-context-3q5.34): bundles show conflict/supersession, this shows repo-state applicability.
- R11 bounds apply: engine work is capped, cancellable, deadline-checked.

## Acceptance
- State-machine tests: current / historical / invalidated / dirty_tree_uncertain each discriminated by fixture repos; rebase and cherry-pick fixtures prove the patch-id fallback.
- Budget test: bounded and cancellable; zero git subprocess on cache hit.
- Read-repair oracle: a failed check writes an invalidation event and the same query stops auto-injecting the row without dreamer involvement.

title: Maturity ladder + taint promotion rules + visibility policy for claims
description:
Feedback-adoption (2026-08 design review). Policy half of the trust model; the trust-class/bitemporal COLUMNS land in U6c (magic-context-3q5.32) — this task consumes them. Recreated after dedup against main (was local U32/3q5.33).

## Goal
Claim lifecycle is an explicit maturity ladder with promotion rules and a visibility policy — repo prose can never become a durable directive; assistant inference can never silently become enforced policy.

## Model
- Taint labels (on U6c source trust class): USER_EXPLICIT, USER_INFERRED, CURRENT_CODE, CURRENT_TEST, CURRENT_CONFIG, REPO_UNTRUSTED_TEXT, TOOL_UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT, ASSISTANT_INFERENCE, DREAMER_INFERENCE.
- Promotion rules: REPO_UNTRUSTED_TEXT / TOOL_UNTRUSTED_OUTPUT may corroborate but never originate a directive-class claim; ASSISTANT/DREAMER inference caps below APPROVED without independent support or explicit user action.
- Maturity ladder distinct from archival status: CANDIDATE -> CORROBORATED -> VERIFIED -> APPROVED -> ENFORCED. Rejected / disputed / contradicted / stale / superseded stay separate epistemic states, not overloaded into one status field.
- Visibility matrix: auto-inject from VERIFIED+; CANDIDATE/CORROBORATED explicit-search only, labeled; ENFORCED points at an artifact (test/policy), not prose.

## Interlocks
- U8: trust_state on retrieval_documents derives from (taint, maturity); KTD19 lane eligibility consumes it.
- U18 (R16): contradicted/quarantined stay hard filters.
- U7 backfill mapping decided with U6c: dreamer-verified rows -> VERIFIED, others -> CORROBORATED (or better mapping with evidence).
- Anti-memory (9o6.1): a hard veto requires VERIFIED+.

## Acceptance
- Promotion-rule unit tests (repo text can never reach APPROVED without USER_EXPLICIT provenance or a verification event).
- Visibility policy is one table-driven function shared by auto-inject and explicit search.

title: [epic] Action-triggered memory: anti-memory, failure signatures, JIT interrupts
description:
The differentiator line vs generic memory providers: surface prior rejections, failure lessons, and safety constraints at the moment the agent is about to repeat them — not as generic prompt injection. Guardrails for the whole line: warn-only (never block), hard per-turn budget, expiry/revalidation via dreamer so warnings don't calcify into stale institutional fear. title: Anti-memory: typed rejected-approach records
description:
Rejected ideas are currently deleted or buried in narrative compartments; retrieval of "we already rejected Redis" depends on luck. Give rejections a first-class type.

## Scope

- Record: trigger (semantic scope of work), rejected_strategy, rejection_reason, safer_alternative (optional), scope, valid_from/valid_until, evidence refs. Rides the claims schema (U6) + bitemporal/trust columns (U6c/3q5.32).

- Surfacing: as a warning fragment when ctx_search / auto-search-hints matches semantically similar work. Warn-only. Later consumed by the JIT interrupt layer.
- Lifecycle: expiry + revalidation in the dreamer verify pass; an anti-memory whose evidence no longer holds is demoted, not silently kept.

## Measure

Repeated-rejected-approach rate, false-warning rate, token overhead. Canary category in U4 (must-never-promote) covers the promotion failure mode.

title: Smart-note evaluator: due-check backlog can starve compilation
description:
select_next_smart_note_evaluation (crates/mc-module/src/smart_note_evaluation.rs) applies strict phase priority (due > compile > liveness > fallback) per claim acquisition. A project with >= MAX_CLAIMS_PER_DRAIN (25) recurring due checks per timer tick consumes every drain iteration with 'due' claims, so notes needing compilation are never selected and stay uncompiled indefinitely despite a healthy evaluator. Raised by codex review on PR #12 (comment 3815004109).

Fix needs a fairness-policy design decision, not a mechanical patch: the selection function is a stateless pure function per acquisition (no drain-scoped state on the Rust side), and its semantics are pinned by the frozen characterization fixture smart-note-evaluation-golden.json (regeneration diff = semantic change requiring review, per PARITY.md). Candidate shapes: (a) per-phase quotas tracked drain-side via a phase hint in the claim request, (b) aging promotion using a 'needs compile since' timestamp (new snapshot/store field), (c) deterministic interleave. Whichever is chosen must update the golden/normative fixtures and PARITY.md.

The worker's per-drain dedup + break bounds the billable loop but cannot reach note 2 (releasing the claim just hands note 1 back). The same fairness redesign should add a re-selection gate (e.g. last_checked_at spacing) to fallback selection alongside the per-phase quota work.

title: Fence module evaluator claim selection by checkout root
description: PR #12 review follow-up (codex 3814664230, claude 3814681244, claude 3814682201): two checkouts/worktrees sharing a root-commit project identity draw from one project-wide pending set, while each worker's filesystem capabilities bind to its own checkout root — so a file-dependent note can be compiled/evaluated against the wrong checkout. Three surfaces share the gap: (1) claim selection carries no originating route root; (2) the dream-timer drain falls back to any same-identity bridge when the exact (identity, root) bridge is missing (deliberate: an undrained module queue is worse, but it widens the wrong-root window); (3) the noteEvaluationAvailable write gate is identity-scoped, consistent with the current model but should tighten to exact-root once claims are fenced. This matches legacy sweep semantics (each registration's sweep evaluated the shared identity-scoped note set against its own root). title: U20: Reranker cascade (explicit search)
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED (U5 gate reaches this unit through its U18 dependency): feature-flagged, DEFAULT OFF; the flag stays off unless the U5 benchmark shows positive reranker lift at acceptable p95. Explicit search only — auto-search NEVER invokes the reranker.

## Goal
Optional quality lift where latency is tolerable.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R11: bounded work.
- R15 boundary (fusion stays the ranking scheme; reranking is a cascade on top for explicit search).
- KTD15: "Reranking is a cascade, explicit search only: cheap contiguous SoA feature model over all candidates -> cross-encoder only for the uncertainty set where score intervals overlap -> token-length batching and a hard deadline. Auto-search never pays reranker latency; it uses exact lookup + FTS + dense + fusion + a conservative confidence gate."
- KTD23: "...a maximum reranker pair/token count (enforced in U20 before cross-encoder dispatch). A deadline alone does not bound planner or reranker work started before it expires."

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/rerank.ts (+ test)
- packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-search/tools.ts
- config schema

## Approach
Feature-flagged, default off until benchmarked.
Stage 1: contiguous SoA feature model (lexical rank, dense rank, exact-match, source type, verification authority, trust, scope, recency, conflict state, supporting-source count, duplicate flag) over all candidates.
Stage 2: cross-encoder only on the uncertainty set (overlapping score intervals), token-length batched, hard deadline, PLUS an explicit maximum pair count and maximum total token count enforced BEFORE dispatch (KTD23) — a wide uncertainty set is capped, not just deadline-bounded, since a deadline alone does not stop unbounded encoding work already queued.

## Test scenarios
- Deadline expiry mid-stage-2 returns the stage-1 ordering (never blocks the tool call).
- Uncertainty-set selection: clearly separated candidates skip stage 2 (encoder spy shows zero calls); overlapping intervals trigger it.
- An uncertainty set wider than the pair/token cap is truncated to the cap BEFORE any cross-encoder call — the encoder never receives more pairs or tokens than the cap allows, independent of the deadline.
- Flag off -> pipeline output IDENTICAL to U18/U19.
- Feature extraction handles missing lanes (dense-off search) without NaN features.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark reports reranker lift; the flag stays off unless lift is positive at acceptable p95.
notes: judge-ruling: U5 gate reaches this unit transitively via U18 - direct edge intentionally omitted per adjudication (minimal graph, gate obligation carried in description); reduce-complexity: two-stage cascade is KTD15-mandated; less-code: default-off flag, no adoption until measured lift - trigger-gated by design, not speculation; perf: pair/token caps enforced BEFORE dispatch (KTD23) so a deadline is not the only bound; ponytail-review: auto-search never invokes it - latency budget protected; invariant-test-review: cap enforcement proven independent of deadline via encoder spy, NaN-free features on missing lanes, flag-off output identity; test-strategy: spy-based examples + flag-off identity golden

title: U19: Dedup + token-budget packing
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED (U5 gate reaches this unit through its U18 dependency): benchmark duplicate-rate and tokens-per-useful-result must improve vs baseline. Note: U18's fusion-parity success criterion is measured on THIS unit's packed output.

## Goal
Delivered context maximizes usefulness per token.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R20: "Final packing deduplicates exact and near-duplicate results (preserving independent provenance as cluster metadata), merges overlapping ordinal intervals, and selects under a token budget by marginal utility per token."

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/result-packing.ts (+ test)
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts
- packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-search/tools.ts

## Approach
1. Collapse exact normalized hashes; SimHash/MinHash near-duplicate clusters with provenance preserved as cluster metadata; merge overlapping session ordinal intervals.
2. Greedy/CELF selection under the token budget; coverage of query atoms/claims/episodes/artifacts as bitsets so marginal gain is AND-NOT + POPCNT-style cheap.

## Test scenarios
- Two near-identical memories (one-word diff) form one cluster; output carries both provenances once.
- Overlapping compartment/message intervals merge; non-overlapping stay distinct.
- A budget of N tokens is NEVER exceeded (property test over random result sets); a higher-marginal-utility item displaces a duplicative higher-scored item.
- Empty results and single-result inputs pass through unchanged.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark duplicate-rate and tokens-per-useful-result improve vs baseline.
notes:
judge-ruling: U5 gate reaches this unit transitively via U18 - direct edge intentionally omitted per adjudication (minimal graph, gate obligation carried in description); reduce-complexity: bitset coverage keeps marginal-gain computation cheap - perf-first shape; less-code: minimal; ponytail-review: SimHash/MinHash scoped to near-dup clustering only; invariant-test-review: budget cap proven as a PROPERTY over random result sets, displacement oracle discriminates utility-vs-score; test-strategy: property test for the budget invariant + examples for cluster/merge edges
DELTA (future-enhancements review): packing objective gains a facet-coverage term — at least one item per unresolved query facet from the U16 query AST; penalize near-duplicates that answer the same facet. Prevents five similar memories all answering one part of a three-part question. Benchmark-gated under U5.

title: U17: Claims-native lexical index replacement
description:
Phase 4. Benchmark-gated lexical replacement.

## Goal
Build the new prose and identifier lexical lanes over `retrieval_documents`. The new lanes are the only query path in the supported release.

## Rules
- Use the U16 query AST and the U8 retrieval projection.
- Parallel table construction is allowed as an internal atomic-build technique.
- Do not keep `storage-memory-fts.ts` query paths live.
- Do not preserve a Porter-era query path, old ranking mode, or flag-off compatibility behavior.
- Once the new tables are validated, activate them and drop the old tables in the same cutover. Old databases are unsupported.

## Approach
1. Build prose FTS with the new tokenizer and weights.
2. Build identifier/path indexes and exact lookup tables.
3. Populate from the claims-native retrieval projection.
4. Use a high-water catch-up only to make the new build internally complete before activation, not to support two runtime query paths.
5. Remove old lexical modules and compatibility flags after the atomic activation.

## Test scenarios
- New index has complete canonical documents and identifiers.
- New query path returns expected results for prose, paths, symbols, SHAs, and short supported needles.
- Concurrent writes are present after activation.
- No test requires serving the old table during construction.

## Verification
- U5 benchmark gate passes.
- Static search finds no production import of the old lexical query path.
acceptance_criteria: New lexical indexes are the only production query path; old FTS query modules and tables are deleted; U5 gate passes.
notes: Removed KTD29 coexistence requirement. Atomic staging is allowed; old query paths, tables, and flag-off behavior are not.

title: U18: Global weighted RRF cutover + progressive deepening
description:
Phase 4. Benchmark-gated global weighted RRF.

## Goal
Make weighted reciprocal-rank fusion the only cross-source ranking path.

## Rules
- No RRF feature flag.
- No flag-off legacy ranking.
- No byte-identical legacy-ranking requirement.
- Benchmark comparison happens before merge on a fixture baseline, not at runtime.
- New sources enter the same fusion contract immediately.

## Approach
1. Apply trust and conflict eligibility before ranks enter fusion.
2. Use one global RRF formula with versioned lane weights.
3. Deepen lanes only while unseen candidates can still beat the current result boundary.
4. Delete cosine/BM25 arithmetic mixing, static source boosts, and old scoring code.
5. Keep only bounded error handling. A failed new engine call fails closed or returns a typed error; it does not select the old ranker.

## Test scenarios
- Fused metrics meet U5 thresholds on final packed output.
- Excluded candidates never affect ranks.
- Progressive deepening stops only when its bound proves safe.
- Every search call uses the new ranker.

## Verification
- No runtime configuration selects the old ranker.
- Old scoring modules and flag-off tests are deleted.
acceptance_criteria: No runtime flag selects old scoring; U5 benchmark passes; old ranker and flag-off tests are deleted.
notes: Removed RRF flag-off compatibility. New weighted RRF is the only ranker in the supported release.

title: U16: Query analyzer + planner + index-time DF
description:
Phase 4 — Query pipeline and ranking. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; verification requires no quality regression vs baseline on the judged corpus for lexical-heavy categories.

## Goal
One lexer + AST drives every lane; plans avoid work.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R17: "A deterministic query analyzer lexes queries into typed atoms (memory ID, commit SHA, file path, symbol, error code, quoted phrase, prose) and selects a plan per query; exact identifiers resolve via indexed lookup without embedding, and dense retrieval is skipped or deferred when lexical confidence is strong."
- KTD8: "The query analyzer is one maximal-munch lexer producing typed atoms and a query AST reused everywhere — exact lookup, FTS query formation, dense gating, highlighting, fusion weighting, packing coverage. Document frequencies are maintained at index time (exact hashed counts for important atoms; a Count-Min Sketch is acceptable where overestimation only downweights a probe) — no query-time posting-count queries. Extends packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/literal-probes.ts rather than a parallel implementation."
- KTD23: the query-atom cap (landed in U3) is enforced in THIS lexer before planning.

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/query-analyzer.ts (+ test), absorbing/extending literal-probes.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts
- DF bookkeeping in the projection writer (retrieval-projection.ts)

## Approach
1. Maximal-munch lexer -> typed atoms (memory ID, SHA, file path, symbol including camelCase/underscore/namespaced forms, error code, quoted phrase, temporal term, prose word); the AST is reused for exact lookup, FTS query formation, dense gating, highlighting, fusion, packing coverage.
2. Plan selection: exact IDs -> indexed lookup, no embedding; rare atoms with strong margin -> FTS first, dense skipped/deferred; mixed -> lexical first, dense conditional; prose -> parallel lanes. Dense embedding no longer starts unconditionally.
3. DF maintained at index time (exact for important atoms, CMS acceptable); no query-time posting counts.

## Test scenarios
- Lexer goldens: scaleConvolveVSym3, foo::bar, CR-297402306, packages/plugin/src/search.ts, HTTP_503, quoted phrases, mixed prose+identifier queries — each yields the expected atom types; identifiers are NOT split at underscores/dots.
- Memory-ID query plan performs ZERO embedding calls (provider spy).
- Rare-atom query with strong lexical margin skips the dense lane; an ambiguous query runs both.
- DF counts update on document add/remove; CMS overestimation only ever DOWNWEIGHTS a probe (property assertion on probe weighting).
- Empty and whitespace-only queries return empty plans without lane execution.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark shows no quality regression vs baseline on the judged corpus for lexical-heavy categories.
notes:
reduce-complexity: one lexer reused by every lane REPLACES parallel probe logic - net complexity reduction; less-code: extends literal-probes.ts rather than a parallel implementation (KTD8); perf: index-time DF kills query-time posting scans, plans avoid work (dense no longer unconditional); ponytail-review: CMS only where overestimation is safe - already scoped; invariant-test-review: CMS safety proven as a property (overestimation only downweights), zero-embedding plan proven via provider spy; test-strategy: golden lexer examples + property for CMS + spy-based plan assertions
DELTA (future-enhancements review): the planner emits ABSTAIN as a first-class plan outcome (low top-score margin + low lane agreement + unresolved claim conflict) instead of always returning best-effort results. Benchmark-gated via the must-abstain canary category added to U4.

title: U15: Benchmark-gated layout/cascade/batching variants
description:
Phase 3. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; every variant here lands ONLY on a measured win vs the U10 baseline (R28). Success-criteria coupling: the 128 MB decoded-index target is CONTINGENT on a U15 compressed variant winning its recall gate; if none passes, the memory threshold relaxes to the f32 baseline (~154 MB) and R12's ANN trigger fires (ANN itself stays deferred/trigger-gated — no HNSW work here).

## Goal
Measure the hardware bets; adopt only winners.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R28: "Hardware-level bets (AoSoA layout, int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix cascades, GEMM micro-batching, mmap layouts) land only on measured wins against the row-major f32 exact baseline with stable tie-breaking, reporting recall and ranking quality for every approximate variant."
- KTD10: "AoSoA block-transposed layout, int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix cascades (conservative Cauchy-Schwarz pruning: skip when prefix_dot + query_tail_norm x candidate_tail_norm < kth_score, tail norms stored per candidate), and GEMM-style micro-batching of concurrent queries are benchmark-gated variants behind the same trait."
- Plan risk note (small-K reality check): "Top-K specialization and micro-batching pay off only under load; U12/U15 measure before adopting."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/ (variant modules + benches)

## Approach
Implement behind the VectorIndex trait and bench against the row-major exact baseline across the U5 matrix:
(a) AoSoA block-transposed layout;
(b) int8/f16 and Matryoshka-prefix cascade with tail-norm Cauchy-Schwarz pruning and oversampled full-f32 rerank;
(c) GEMM-style micro-batching for concurrent same-generation queries with a scheduler choosing shard-one-query / independent / batch (no added latency for isolated interactive queries).
Adopt per measured win; document losers and REMOVE their code (dead variants do not ship).

## Test scenarios
- Cascade preserves EXACT top-K on the comparator corpus when exact-mode pruning is enabled (tolerance-aware float handling asserted).
- Quantized recall reported per configuration; any recall < 1.0 variant is marked approximate and EXCLUDED from exact mode.
- Batching: 4 concurrent queries on one generation read vector pages once (bytes-touched counter) and match serial results.

## Verification
- Bench report vs the U10 baseline committed; only winning variants remain enabled.
notes: reduce-complexity: three bets behind the existing trait, no new seams; less-code: losers deleted, not flag-parked (plan-mandated); perf: this unit IS the measured-perf discipline (R28); ponytail-review: micro-batching pays only under load - measured before adopting per plan risk note; invariant-test-review: exact-mode cascade oracle = exact top-K preservation with tolerance-aware float compare, approximate variants must report recall and are excluded from exact mode; test-strategy: comparator property + bytes-touched counters + bench-gated adoption

title: U13: Module routes + TS client + queues/cancellation
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
The engine is reachable from both harnesses with deadlines, priorities, a transparent fallback, and a caller-authorization boundary that cannot be bypassed by a mis-scoped filter or a coalesced request.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R11: bounded, cancellable, priority-aware; "interactive queries have reserved capacity that backfills and background work cannot consume."
- R13: "Search stays functional when the Rust engine is unavailable (daemon down, rust mode off, index cold): the TypeScript scan path remains a working fallback, and cold-start windows degrade transparently."
- R32: "The dense search route derives a caller's authorized project/session/trust scope server-side and never trusts a caller-supplied filter as authorization; every coalescing key (singleflight, result cache) includes that authorized scope so two callers with the same query text but different scope never share a scan or a cached result."
- KTD25: "Singleflight and the generation-keyed result cache key on the authorized scope, the complete normalized filter set, the embedding space, and the generation id together — never on (embedding_space, normalized_query_hash) alone." Plan risk note: this key shape is a correctness requirement, not a performance nicety.
- KTD1 (routes on the existing ck-mc module; subc transport 0.28-0.38 ms p50), KTD3 (dedicated compute pool; cancellation between scan blocks), KTD16 (the native ctx_search facade in crates/mc-module/src/memory_tool.rs routes through the SAME engine; divergences documented per PARITY.md conventions only when mechanism, not behavior, differs).

## Key files
- crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs (route registration), new crates/mc-module/src/vector_search.rs, crates/mc-module/src/memory_tool.rs
- packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-transport.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search-backend.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts

## Approach
1. vector.search route: accepts query text or vector, filters, K, embedding-space identity, deadline; inference, normalization, scan, top-K stay daemon-side; cancellation checked between scan blocks.
2. Per KTD25: derive the caller's authorized project/session/trust scope server-side and intersect it with requested filters; coalescing keys include authorized scope + complete normalized filter set + embedding space + generation id.
3. Bounded interactive and background queues with reserved interactive capacity.
4. TS search-backend.ts seam: RustVectorBackend (route) and TsScanBackend (current scalar path) behind one interface; automatic fallback on connection failure/staleness per module-transport.ts conventions; a cold daemon serves the TS fallback while segments load, then flips.
5. Native ctx_search facade routes through the same engine (KTD16).

## Test scenarios
- Route round-trip on the hermetic daemon harness (packages/e2e-tests/src/rust-harness.ts, crates/mc-module/tests/real_daemon.rs): identical results TS-fallback vs Rust route on a seeded corpus.
- Two callers with the same query text but DIFFERENT authorized project scope never share a coalesced scan or a cached result (singleflight/cache-key fixture with deliberately colliding query hashes and differing scope).
- A request whose caller-supplied filter widens beyond the caller's authorized scope is served only the authorized subset, never the wider requested one.
- Deadline shorter than scan time: route returns cancelled; TS caller degrades per auto-search semantics (hint skipped, no error surfaced to user).
- Daemon down: backend seam falls back to TS scan with one loud log; results still returned.
- Two identical concurrent queries from the SAME authorized scope: one inference + one scan (singleflight counters).
- Background backfill saturating queues: an interactive query is still admitted within reserved capacity (latency assertion under load).
- Cold start: first search after daemon restart serves fallback; post-warm search serves the Rust path (state visible via status route).

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace + bun test + hermetic e2e group green.
notes: reduce-complexity: unit is OVERSIZED (routes + authz + queues + fallback + facade) - noted per conversion constraints, not split; less-code: TsScanBackend reuses the existing scalar path behind the seam, no rewrite; perf: reserved interactive capacity asserted under load; ponytail-review: lean given R32/KTD25 key shape is load-bearing security, not a nicety; invariant-test-review: scope-isolation oracle uses deliberately colliding query hashes with differing scope - proves the R32 key shape, widened-filter test asserts served subset; test-strategy: hermetic e2e + counter-based singleflight oracles + adversarial fixtures

title: U14: Segment persistence + outbox consumer (push route)
description:
Phase 3. Crash-consistency tests are a hard gate for this unit (Verification Contract: crash suites for U14).

## Goal
Index generations survive restarts and stay fresh via the outbox — no full rebuild per insert — without the module opening context.db directly.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R14: "Vector index generations are immutable (base segment + bounded delta segments + tombstone bitmap), published atomically via a manifest; readers never observe a partial build, and old generations retire only after readers drain."
- R6 (transactional outbox maintenance), R31 (no new daemon; converge on existing machinery).
- KTD11: "Readers hold Arc<Mmap>-style generations; publish via manifest/ArcSwap; size-tiered compaction; per-segment local top-K merged at the end. Avoids full-generation rebuilds on every insert."
- KTD30: "U14's outbox consumer receives batches through a TS-initiated push route, not by the module opening context.db. The TS projection writer calls a vector.ingest route (established by U13) with pending outbox batches; the module writes segments and returns acknowledgment IDs; TS marks those outbox rows applied. crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs states the module never opens or attaches context.db, and that boundary changes only at U29's authority convergence — U14 does not anticipate it."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/segments.rs, src/manifest.rs (new)
- crates/mc-module/src/vector_search.rs; new vector.ingest route in crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs
- TS-side outbox drain in packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/retrieval-projection.ts

## Approach
1. Immutable base + bounded delta segments + tombstone bitmap; atomic manifest publish (fsync -> validate -> swap); readers pin generations; retire on drain; size-tiered compaction.
2. Per KTD30 (quoted above); acknowledgment is batched (no per-row transactions) on both sides.
3. Per-project/space byte-bounded residency with LRU eviction (replaces the process-global 256 MB decoded-pool behavior with an explicit budget).

## Test scenarios
- kill -9 between fsync and manifest swap: reopen serves the OLD generation intact (crash test with fault-injection points) — the R14 no-partial-reads oracle.
- Compaction removes tombstoned ordinals; post-compaction search equals pre-compaction search minus deletions (comparator).
- A reader holding an old generation during publish completes its scan on the old data; the next query sees the new generation.
- An outbox batch of N mutations pushed over vector.ingest lands in <= ceil(N/batch) transactions on the module side (statement counter), and applied_at marks EXACTLY ONCE on the TS side even under redelivery (idempotent ack test).
- The module process never issues a SQLite connection open against context.db during this unit's tests (process-level assertion) — the KTD30 boundary oracle.
- Eviction: exceeding the byte budget evicts the LRU project; the next query for it reloads from segments, correctness preserved.

## Verification
- cargo test; crash-consistency tests in CI; staleness SLA documented on the route (outbox consumed on search when pending, bounded added latency).
notes: reduce-complexity: segment machinery is R14-mandated; less-code: replaces the process-global 256MB decoded pool with one explicit budget; perf: batched acks kill per-row transactions (R29 direction); ponytail-review: no anticipation of U29 boundary change - module never opens context.db, held by process-level assertion; invariant-test-review: R14 no-partial-reads proven by kill-9 between fsync and manifest swap serving the OLD generation, exactly-once ack under redelivery; test-strategy: crash/fault-injection form + comparator + statement counters

title: U12: Kernel dispatch + top-K selection benchmarks
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Runtime-dispatched kernels and a measured top-K structure choice.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R28: measure, do not assume — variants land only on measured wins.
- KTD2: safe-SIMD-first with "runtime-dispatched NEON and AVX2/FMA variants (AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed) and no blanket target-cpu=native".

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/kernels.rs, src/topk.rs, benches/

## Approach
1. Kernel set: portable scalar, NEON (+dot-product extension where present), AVX2/FMA; feature-detected dispatch at index-open; no target-cpu=native artifacts.
2. Top-K candidates: fixed-capacity sorted array, binary heap, buffered select_nth_unstable — benched at K in {5, 32, 100}; the winner per K-band becomes the default. Losing structures do not ship as dead code (global Definition of Done: no dead experiment code).
3. Consecutive-window group max: retain max while walking (compartment_id, window_index) order instead of map+sort.

## Test scenarios
- All kernels agree with scalar EXACTLY (shared comparator harness from U10).
- Dispatch on a host lacking a feature falls back cleanly (force-disable flag in tests).
- Top-K structures agree with a full-sort reference across K values and duplicate scores.

## Verification
- cargo test; bench table (kernel x dims, structure x K) in the PR.
notes: reduce-complexity: ok; less-code: losing top-K structures REMOVED after measurement, only the winner ships (no dead experiment code); perf: measured K-band selection is the whole point; ponytail-review: AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed (KTD2), nothing speculative built; invariant-test-review: exact-agreement oracle vs scalar comparator including duplicate-score ties, force-disable fallback test; test-strategy: comparator property harness reused from U10 + bench table

title: U10: mc-vector crate: exact engine + trait
description:
Phase 3 — Rust dense engine. Develops in parallel with Phase 2 against synthetic corpora; integration comes in U13. Ships no ranking change itself, but its criterion baseline is the R28 correctness comparator that U15 measures against.

## Goal
The ID-first exact engine exists as a standalone crate with the VectorIndex abstraction.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R9: "Hot-path dense search runs in Rust over contiguous normalized vectors and returns compact (ordinal, score) pairs; stable IDs, text, and metadata hydrate only after fusion selects final candidates."
- R12: "Exact search is the default engine. ANN (HNSW) is added only behind the VectorIndex abstraction when measured thresholds are crossed: auto-search p95 above ~25 ms or active decoded index above ~128 MB for a scope." This unit lands the abstraction SEAM only — no HNSW work.
- R14: in-memory generation shape (immutable generation + tombstones).
- KTD1: "Dense engine lives in a new crates/mc-vector crate, exposed as routes on the existing ck-mc module ... mc-vector depends only on workspace-internal crates (no subc/cortexkit deps) so it builds and benches in isolation."
- KTD2: "Safe-SIMD-first kernels with runtime dispatch. The workspace is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] everywhere; mc-vector starts with a safe SIMD abstraction (pulp or wide) over a portable scalar baseline ... Unsafe is admitted only if benchmarks prove the safe abstraction leaves large wins on the table."
- KTD3: "Shard-local top-K per worker, merge workers x K; cancellation checked between scan blocks; never a shared heap in the scan loop."
- KTD10: "Row-major f32 exact scan is the baseline and correctness comparator."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/ (new: src/lib.rs, src/generation.rs, src/scan.rs, src/topk.rs, src/scratch.rs, criterion benches under benches/)
- root Cargo.toml workspace member

## Approach
1. Generation structure: packed normalized f32 row-major matrix, stable_ids: Vec<u64> (cold), filter bitmaps, tombstone bitset, group ranges (compartment -> ordinal range), generation id. QueryScratch with scores, seen-epoch, touched list, fixed-capacity top-K.
2. Dense u32 ordinals internally; (ordinal, score) output; stable-ID conversion only after top-K.
3. Normalize on index, normalize query once, dot product only; shard-local top-K, merge workers x K on a dedicated compute pool (KTD3).
4. VectorIndex trait: search(partition, query, k, filters, deadline), build_generation(docs), publish_generation(gen); ExactIndex is the first impl.
5. Scalar reference implementation kept as the correctness comparator; safe-SIMD kernels via pulp/wide (KTD2).
Directional: exact top-K with stable tie-breaking (score desc, ordinal asc).

## Test scenarios
- Property-test comparison: random corpus (1k x {128,384,1024}), random queries — SIMD scan top-K equals the scalar reference EXACTLY under stable tie-breaking, with and without tombstones.
- Deleted (tombstoned) ordinals never appear in results.
- K > live corpus returns all live, sorted.
- Deadline expiring mid-scan returns a cancelled error, NOT partial results presented as complete.
- Zero-vector and duplicate-vector inputs behave (no NaN; duplicates tie-break by ordinal).
- cargo bench baseline recorded for the scan across the U5 matrix dims.

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace; cargo clippy -- -D warnings; criterion baseline committed as a snapshot for U15 comparisons.
notes: reduce-complexity: VectorIndex trait seam is R12-mandated for future ANN, not speculative; less-code: scalar reference doubles as the correctness comparator - not dead code; perf: criterion baseline IS a deliverable (R28 comparator); ponytail-review: no HNSW, no unsafe - both trigger-gated per plan; invariant-test-review: SIMD-vs-scalar exact-equality property oracle under stable tie-breaking, deadline test asserts cancelled error rather than silent partials; test-strategy: property-based comparator + example edge cases (zero-vector, duplicates, K over corpus)

title: U11: Bitmap filters + adaptive scan
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Filters cut memory traffic, not just results.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R10: "Filtering (project, session, source type, trust, status, embedding space, time/ordinal range) uses bitmaps applied before or inside the scan so excluded vectors never touch the memory hierarchy; the scan strategy adapts to filter selectivity (dense masked scan, sparse gather, or segment skip)."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/filter.rs (new), src/scan.rs

## Approach
1. Bitmaps per project/session/source/trust/status/space + coarse ordinal/time ranges; raw bitsets for dense sets, Roaring-style containers for sparse; the crossover is MEASURED per architecture (bench, not assumed).
2. Strategy selection by allowed-set density: dense -> sequential masked scan; sparse -> set-bit enumeration + gather; range-restricted -> whole-segment skip via min/max metadata.

## Test scenarios
- Each strategy returns IDENTICAL results to the reference filter-then-scan for random filter sets at 0.1% / 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% selectivity.
- Segment-skip: a query restricted to an ordinal range touches only overlapping segments (assert via scan counters).
- Empty filter set returns empty WITHOUT touching vectors.
- Bench records bytes-touched per selectivity point — proves the R10 mechanism (excluded vectors are not read), not just output correctness.

## Verification
- cargo test; bench comparison in PR notes.
notes: reduce-complexity: three strategies are R10-mandated adaptivity; less-code: minimal; perf: bytes-touched counter proves the mechanism (excluded vectors never read), not just outputs; ponytail-review: raw-vs-Roaring crossover measured per architecture, not assumed - already gated; invariant-test-review: strategy-equivalence property vs reference filter-then-scan across selectivities + counter-based traffic oracle; test-strategy: property comparison + mechanism counters

title: U9: Verify direct cutover and remove legacy surfaces
description:
Phase 2. Direct claims cutover verification and legacy-surface removal.

## Goal
Prove that the direct cutover is complete and remove any remaining compatibility surface. This is not a delayed reader migration. U7 and U8 already use claims and the claims-native retrieval projection.

## Scope
- Re-point search, mural, dreamer, module state-sync, dashboard/TUI, and native module routes to claim current-state and retrieval documents.
- Remove mutable semantic `memories` reads and writes, compatibility crosswalks, backfill runners, old embedding tables, and compatibility-only schema guards.
- Remove legacy result-ID adapters, old memory-shaped wire payloads, and compatibility feature flags.
- Keep only fail-closed schema-version checks and correctness-preserving atomic index staging. Do not preserve an old implementation for rollback.

## Test scenarios
- Fresh fixture outputs match the claims-native expected results.
- Search, mural, dreamer, module, dashboard, and Pi/OpenCode paths contain no legacy fallback.
- Static reference scan finds no production import of compatibility modules.
- Direct writes to removed legacy tables fail because the tables do not exist.
- Unsupported old databases fail closed with an actionable reset message.

## Verification
- Full bun, cargo, plugin, Pi, CLI, dashboard, and e2e suites pass.
- The final schema and dependency graph contain one semantic write/read approach.
acceptance_criteria: All readers and wire/dashboard paths use claims; compatibility modules, tables, flags, and old payloads are removed; fresh-schema and static reference checks pass.
notes: This is cleanup and verification, not a delayed coexistence phase. U7 and U8 must already be claims-native.

title: U8: Claims-native retrieval projection and embedding spaces
description:
Phase 2. Claims-native retrieval projection, outbox, generations, and embedding spaces.

## Goal
Build every retrieval document and index from authoritative claims, revisions, evidence, tool events, notes, commits, and other current sources. The new projection is the only search representation.

## Governing constraints
- Retrieval structures remain rebuildable derived projections.
- Vectors remain content-addressed by embedding space, text view, and content hash.
- Index maintenance uses transactional outbox rows and per-scope generations.
- No old embedding tables, legacy memory projection, dual-read path, or compatibility adapter remains live.

## Approach
1. Create `retrieval_documents`, `document_embeddings`, postings, `index_outbox`, and `search_index_generation` from the new schema.
2. Populate memory documents from claim current revisions and evidence, not `memories` rows.
3. Build indexes from a fresh claims-native corpus. Do not preserve `memory_embeddings`, `compartment_chunk_embeddings`, or `git_commit_embeddings` for later reader migration.
4. Make claim mutations publish projection effects in the same transaction boundary required by U7.
5. Provide a rebuild command from authoritative tables and prove equality against a fresh build.
6. Use atomic staging and activation for index construction, but do not serve an old query path or retain an old ranking path.

## Test scenarios
- Fresh claim revision produces exactly one retrieval document effect and generation update.
- Rebuild produces identical document identities, content hashes, and postings.
- Duplicate content shares one physical vector within an embedding space.
- Corrupt derived indexes rebuild without changing claims.
- No legacy embedding or memory-projection table is read by production search.

## Verification
- Migration, projection, outbox rollback, generation, rebuild, and embedding-space tests pass.
- Search starts on the new projection without a compatibility mode.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh claims-native projection, outbox, generations, embeddings, rebuild, and rollback tests pass; no legacy embedding or memory projection table is read.
notes: Direct cutover: retrieval projection is built from claims and current sources. Do not retain old embedding tables or compatibility query paths.

title: U7: Direct claims cutover for memory storage
description:
Phase 2. Direct claims cutover for memory storage.

## Goal
Claims become the only semantic source of truth. All memory writers and readers use the claims/revision/evidence API from their first supported release.

There are no legacy callers, deployed users, or existing databases to preserve. Do not implement memories-to-claims backfill, dual-read, a maintained `memories` compatibility projection, legacy IDs, or a later reader migration.

## Scope
- Make claims/revisions/evidence the storage API for OpenCode, Pi, dreamer, historian, module mirror, dashboard, identity merge, relocation, verification, and session paths.
- Use operation envelopes for retries and request-key reuse detection.
- Commit claim revisions, evidence, lifecycle state, outbox effects, and generations atomically.
- Replace mutable memory IDs with canonical claim/revision/retrieval-document identities at API boundaries.
- Update the module wire and dashboard/TUI payloads to new claim-native shapes in this cutover.
- Delete `legacy_memory_claims`, `claim_backfill_*`, `hasMemoryClaimsCompatSchema`, `storage-memory-projection.ts`, and compatibility-only guards and startup runners.
- Treat old `context.db` files and old binaries as unsupported. Reset or refuse them; do not migrate them.

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claims.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/context-authority.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/relocate-memory.ts
- packages/pi-plugin/src/tools/ctx-memory.ts
- packages/cli/src/commands/doctor*.ts

## Test scenarios
- Every semantic write creates or appends claim state with one atomic commit.
- Every reader uses claim current-state and evidence.
- A fresh database has no mutable semantic `memories` source.
- No production SQL path reads or writes compatibility tables.
- Crash injection proves no partial claim/evidence/outbox/generation commit.
- Replayed operations return the stored result without duplicate effects.
- Unsupported old databases fail closed.

## Verification
- Full plugin, Pi, CLI, dashboard, and e2e suites pass on fresh databases.
- Static search finds no legacy memory compatibility branch or reader.
design: Implement the claims-only greenfield cutover. Rewire every writer, reader, wire boundary, and dashboard path together; remove memories compatibility tables, backfill, dual-read branches, and old IDs. Preserve only atomicity, replay safety, and fail-closed fences.
acceptance_criteria: All writers and readers use claims-native APIs; no compatibility tables or backfill runner; fresh database has no mutable semantic memories source; crash and replay tests pass; unsupported old DBs fail closed.
notes: Supersedes dual-read/backfill design. User confirmed greenfield conditions: no legacy callers, deployed users, or existing databases. Claims-only cutover is required.

title: U6: Claims/evidence authoritative schema
description:
Phase 2. Claims and evidence domain.

## Goal
Make claims, revisions, evidence, conflicts, and verification events the only semantic storage contract for fresh databases.

This is a greenfield cutover. There are no supported legacy callers, deployed users, or legacy databases to migrate. Do not add a compatibility projection, dual-read API, or memory-row backfill.

## Scope
- Create the authoritative claims/evidence schema and numeric project identity registry.
- Enforce immutable revisions, evidence links, current-revision CAS, project ownership, and fail-closed corruption reads.
- Expose transaction-local writers and current-state readers for every new caller.
- Reject unsupported old schema versions and old binaries. Refusal is a safety fence, not a compatibility contract.

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/storage-claims-schema.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claims.ts
- migration and schema-fence tests

## Approach
1. Build the claims schema for the new database shape.
2. Make claims/revisions/evidence writes atomic and append-only.
3. Do not seed claims from `memories`; fresh fixtures create claims directly.
4. Remove assumptions that a mutable memory row is authoritative.

## Test scenarios
- Fresh database creates only the new semantic schema.
- Claim creation and revision append preserve prior bytes.
- Stale current-revision writes roll back without partial rows.
- Direct SQL corruption is detected or rejected.
- Unsupported old schema versions fail closed.

## Verification
- Claims schema, migration, fence, and corruption tests pass.
- No production caller reads or writes legacy memory state.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh claims schema and project registry; immutable revision/evidence/CAS tests pass; unsupported old schemas fail closed; no production caller reads or writes legacy memory state.
notes: Greenfield decision: claims are the only semantic source. No legacy memory rows, compatibility projection, dual-read, or backfill. Old schema and old binaries fail closed.

title: Retain skipped frames in RawClient::frames_until_corr
description:
The test support helper `RawClient::frames_until_corr` returns the frames it consumed while searching, but most call sites discard them with `let (_, response) = ...`. Those frames are the only copy, so a later sequential call for a correlation whose response was already consumed waits out its whole budget.

This produced one real flake, fixed in 29e6f4a1 by having `pipelined_shutdown_requests_on_one_connection_both_settle` read the second response out of the returned list. The remaining exposure is latent: a stray bootstrap `Ping` gets skipped during TCP negotiation, which is harmless because `frames_until_corr` already excludes `TY_PING` from matching and no test asserts on the resulting Pong.

The durable fix is to stop discarding the skipped frames — buffer them on the client so a later `frames_until_corr` searches the buffer before reading the socket — and audit every call site together rather than adding local exceptions. Doing that per-site is what allowed one flake to exist already.
acceptance_criteria: Consumed non-matching frames are buffered and reachable by a later search; every frames_until_corr call site audited; the pipelined-shutdown test still passes without its local lookaside.

title: Extract shared PID start-time probes for reuse by the Rust e2e reaper
description:
packages/e2e-tests/src/rust-runner/hermetic-mc-host.ts has processStartTimeMs and processExecutable for leak reaping, which overlap with packages/plugin/src/shared/rpc-utils.ts.

The overlap is not directly reusable as it stands. isPidIdentityPlausible takes an RpcPortFileRecord and its legacy fallback asks whether the command looks like OpenCode, which is the wrong oracle for a fixture process identified by its executable path. The genuinely shared primitives, readLinuxProcessStartTime and readPsProcessStartTime, are module-private in rpc-utils.ts, and the harness reads a procfs exe realpath rather than a command name on purpose.

The convergence worth having: export the start-time probes (procfs fast path plus ps fallback, one skew-tolerance constant) as a record-shape-agnostic helper, and have both callers layer their own identity oracle on top. That removes the duplicated ps parsing and the harness s hardcoded 5000 ms tolerance without forcing the OpenCode command heuristic into the fixture reaper.
acceptance_criteria: Both callers use one start-time probe; each keeps its own identity predicate; rpc-utils test hooks still work.

title: Select a benchmark-approved GPU model without mixing embedding spaces
description:
## Context
GPU availability can justify a larger or different embedding model, but model choice changes the embedding space. Hardware detection alone is not evidence that a model improves retrieval. Existing 3q5 tasks already own embedding-space identity, provider capabilities, judged evaluation, lazy backfill, and gated default swaps.

## Current State
- `packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding-identity.ts:10-79` includes Synapse model and fingerprint in provider identity.
- `packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding-synapse.ts` discovers one certified model and validates model/fingerprint/epoch/dimensions on every response.
- `magic-context-3q5.25` expands identity to the full embedding-space contract.
- `magic-context-3q5.27` benchmarks candidate models and owns any default swap.

## Desired State
Trusted startup selection chooses exactly one certified Synapse lane:
- GPU bundle/model when policy allows it, hardware and runtime eligibility pass, and the model is approved by `magic-context-3q5.27`.
- Certified CPU bundle/model under the documented unsupported/unavailable behavior.

The active lane publishes one exact model identity through the existing catalog and `models.list`. If CPU and GPU profiles differ in any embedding-space field, they use distinct space IDs, generations, vectors, and lazy backfills. Search never compares vectors across spaces.

## Implementation Guidance
Extend startup configuration and lane initialization. Reuse existing discovery, model metadata, destination model IDs, generation checks, shadow lane, and lazy backfill. Do not add request-time device/model selection or a general multi-model registry.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **REUSE / EXTEND**.
- REUSE `magic-context-3q5.25` embedding-space identity and `.27` benchmark/cutover.
- EXTEND `SynapseConfig` and existing one-lane initialization only as specified by the forged plan.
- REUSE existing fallback-provider behavior only for explicit Synapse failure. Never persist fallback vectors under the Synapse identity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Startup policy is deterministic and testable for supported GPU, unsupported GPU, missing driver, invalid GPU bundle, invalid CPU bundle, and forced modes.
- [ ] GPU model activation requires a committed `magic-context-3q5.27` benchmark decision; otherwise the CPU model remains active.
- [ ] Catalog and `models.list` expose only the active certified lane and its exact execution/model identity.
- [ ] A model/profile change opens a new embedding space and generation; old vectors remain isolated and retire through existing lazy backfill/GC.
- [ ] Partial re-embedding serves lexical results for gaps and performs no cross-space cosine comparison.
- [ ] GPU disappearance across restarts selects the documented CPU path without relabeling old GPU vectors.
- [ ] Runtime GPU failure never causes same-request CPU substitution.
- [ ] No new model registry, benchmark harness, or recovery scheduler is introduced.

## Testing Strategy
Use a startup matrix with fake hardware/runtime probes, then run existing shadow/cutover fixtures against different model dimensions and fingerprints. Include downgrade and rollback across process restarts.

## Related Work
Hard dependencies: `magic-context-3q5.25`, `magic-context-3q5.27`, and bounded GPU runtime. Related: `magic-context-3q5.26`, `magic-context-pml.4`.

title: Package, diagnose, and smoke the certified GPU Synapse lane
description:

GPU packaging must extend that work.

## Current State
- `packages/cli/src/lib/embedding-runtime.ts:219-363` probes installed ONNX Runtime binaries in a child process and formats doctor failures.
- `packages/plugin/scripts/smoke-mc-host-synapse.ts` drives authenticated discovery, all four operations, restart recovery, and SQLite receipt application.
- `docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` defines offline CPU bundle/runtime verification and production smoke inputs.

## Desired State
Supported installations include one exact, certified GPU runtime package and GPU model bundle, plus the certified CPU path. Doctor reports whether GPU policy is eligible and why it is not. Release smoke proves the selected GPU provider on real hardware with network disabled and proves CPU behavior on a host without eligible GPU support.

## Implementation Guidance
Extend `magic-context-c50.8` install/doctor ownership and the existing Synapse smoke. Reuse subprocess probing so a broken native provider cannot crash the CLI process. Keep native library paths and hashes in trusted installation metadata. Do not download drivers, ORT, CUDA, TensorRT, or models at runtime.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND**. Extend current ORT load probe, Synapse production smoke, bundle documentation, and daemon startup inputs. Do not create a second installer or standalone GPU daemon.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Package matrix names exact supported OS, architecture, GPU, minimum driver, ORT/provider build, dependent native libraries, and hashes.
- [ ] CLI doctor distinguishes no GPU, unsupported GPU, missing driver/library, provider-load failure, insufficient memory, invalid bundle, semantic-certification failure, and healthy GPU lane.
- [ ] Native probing runs in a disposable child process and returns redacted diagnostics.
- [ ] Offline real-GPU smoke passes authentication, discovery, query, batch, pending/pages, ambiguous replay, restart resubmission, atomic destination application, and shutdown cleanup.
- [ ] CPU-only smoke proves documented behavior when GPU is absent or unsupported.
- [ ] Forced GPU mode fails closed when eligibility fails; auto behavior follows the forged policy.
- [ ] Production smoke refuses toy bundles, placeholder hashes, unapproved models, wrong driver/runtime identity, and unexpected execution providers.
- [ ] Release evidence records latency, throughput, peak host/device memory, loaded native libraries, and feature graph.
- [ ] Documentation covers installation, policy, doctor output, rollback, model-space migration, and removal.

## Testing Strategy
Keep fake-probe cases in regular CI. Run real GPU smoke on labeled hardware with the exact packaged artifacts. Run CPU fallback smoke on a GPU-disabled or CPU-only host. Never skip production GPU smoke for a release that claims GPU support.

## Related Work
Depends on model selection and `magic-context-c50.8`. Consumes model approval from `magic-context-3q5.27`.

title: Add certified GPU Synapse execution and hardware-selected model lane
description:
## Context
PR 16 / `magic-context-c50.6` establishes one certified, CPU-only Synapse model behind `mc-host`. The next capability is optional GPU execution and, when approved hardware is present, use of a separately certified GPU-suitable embedding model.

Existing work already owns important parts of this change:
- `magic-context-3q5.25` defines embedding spaces as full identities.
- `magic-context-3q5.26` defines provider/token-aware batching and capacity descriptors.
- `magic-context-3q5.27` evaluates candidate models and gates any default swap on the judged benchmark.
- `magic-context-c50.8` owns daemon/runtime packaging and doctor integration.
- `magic-context-pml.4` later moves the wider embedding pipeline into Rust.

This epic must extend those contracts, not create a second model registry, benchmark framework, recovery queue, or embedding identity.

## Desired State
`mc-host` can start one certified Synapse lane on a supported GPU. Trusted startup configuration supplies certified CPU and GPU runtime/bundle candidates. Startup chooses one lane according to an explicit, documented policy and publishes its exact model, fingerprint, epoch, dimensions, and execution profile.

A different GPU model is eligible only after `magic-context-3q5.27` records an in-domain benchmark win. Switching models creates a distinct embedding space and uses existing lazy backfill/cutover behavior. CPU and GPU vectors never share an identity unless certification proves they are the same embedding space within the accepted tolerance.

CPU remains the supported fallback when GPU hardware, driver, runtime, or certified GPU bundle is unavailable. A failure must never write CPU vectors under a GPU model identity or vice versa.

## Scope
1. Forge the hardware-support, execution-provider, resource-envelope, fallback, and model-selection contract.
2. Extend the certified bundle/native-runtime identity to cover GPU execution and dependencies.
3. Run bounded GPU inference under existing job, cancellation, and shutdown ownership.
4. Select the benchmark-approved GPU model at startup without cross-space comparisons.
5. Package, diagnose, and smoke the certified GPU lane on supported hosts.

## Stop Conditions
- No request-selected model path, runtime library, device, or execution provider.
- No runtime download, mutable model registry, model hot reload, or persistent Rust job queue.
- No multi-GPU scheduling until measurements and a separate task justify it.
- No default-model change without `magic-context-3q5.27` benchmark evidence.
- No silent CPU/GPU substitution under one model identity.

## Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND / REUSE**.

- Extend `SynapseConfig`, `Backend`, `OrtIdentity`, existing job limits, and incarnation tracker in `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/`; do not add a parallel service or queue.
- Reuse Synapse request keys, process-local jobs, `module_restarted`, ledger receipts, and atomic destination application unchanged.
- Reuse `magic-context-3q5.25` embedding-space identity and `magic-context-3q5.27` model evaluation/cutover. Do not add another model-selection database.
- Extend `magic-context-c50.8` runtime packaging and doctor surfaces.

## Success Criteria
- Supported GPU hosts can run an offline, certified Synapse lane through the existing four operations.
- Unsupported or unhealthy GPU hosts use the documented CPU behavior without identity confusion.
- GPU memory, concurrency, batch work, retained results, and shutdown are finitely bounded and tested at exact limits.
- A GPU-specific model activates only after benchmark approval and always opens a distinct embedding space when its contract differs.
- Bun and Node real-host smokes cover GPU selection, CPU fallback, restart, and destination receipt atomicity.

## Related Work
- `magic-context-c50.6`: CPU Synapse baseline.
- `magic-context-c50.8`: daemon/runtime packaging and doctor.
- `magic-context-3q5.25`: embedding-space identity.
- `magic-context-3q5.26`: provider capability and batching contract.
- `magic-context-3q5.27`: model evaluation and gated swap.
- `magic-context-pml.4`: future Rust ownership of the wider embedding pipeline.

title: Forge GPU execution and model-selection contract
description:
## Context
The shipped Synapse design deliberately allows only one CPU execution provider, one inference permit, and one owner-provisioned model bundle. GPU support changes native dependencies, memory ceilings, concurrency, shutdown cost, failure handling, and model identity. Choosing those mechanisms inside an implementation task would anchor the project before their operational cost is known.

## Current State
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:56-191` verifies and commits one process-global ORT library, then builds FastEmbed with one intra-op CPU thread.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:35-81` holds finite host-owned limits and one trusted bundle/ORT configuration.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs:140-160` uses one FIFO semaphore and an incarnation tracker for started native calls.
- `docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` explicitly certifies CPU-only execution and excludes accelerator features.

## Desired State
Produce an implementation-ready, adversarially reviewed plan for the smallest supported GPU profile. The plan must decide the first execution provider and platform matrix, define "GPU supported," measure the operational envelope, and specify deterministic CPU behavior when GPU eligibility fails.

The plan must keep one active Synapse lane per process. It must treat a different GPU model as a distinct embedding space and consume the model winner from `magic-context-3q5.27`, not select a model from public leaderboards or hardware alone.

## Required Decisions
- Initial provider/platform scope, such as CUDA only versus a broader matrix. Do not promise providers that cannot be packaged and tested.
- Trusted startup policy (`auto`, forced CPU, forced GPU, or smaller equivalent) and failure behavior for each mode.
- Hardware eligibility evidence: device, driver, execution-provider availability, model compatibility, and minimum usable memory.
- Exact native artifacts and hashes, including provider dependencies beyond the core ORT library.
- GPU memory accounting, batch/token limits, concurrency/stream count, admission, OOM classification, and shutdown drain bound.
- Whether CPU and GPU execution of the same bundle are one certified space or separate spaces. Require semantic evidence for any shared identity.
- Startup and runtime fault matrix. Never retry a request on a different model or execution profile under the original identity.
- Rollout, rollback, observability, doctor output, and real-hardware test matrix.

## Implementation Guidance
Run `plan-forge` for this feature. Include performance and footgun review. Derive peak resident CPU bytes, peak device bytes, host-to-device copies, work per batch, queueing delay, and worst-case shutdown drain at every proposed cap. Update child bead descriptions if the accepted plan changes their boundaries.

### Existing Code to Reuse
Duplication check outcome: **EXTEND**.
- Extend existing Synapse backend/config/lifecycle. No second service.
- Reuse existing embedding-space, benchmark, and lazy re-embed work in `magic-context-3q5.25` and `.27`.
- Reuse `magic-context-3q5.26` capability descriptors instead of inventing GPU-only batching metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Versioned plan records the selected provider/platform matrix and rejected alternatives.
- [ ] Operational envelope contains explicit CPU memory, GPU memory, batch, concurrency, queue, latency, and shutdown calculations.
- [ ] Plan defines auto/forced selection behavior and every fallback or fail-closed branch.
- [ ] Plan defines model and execution-profile identity, including when re-embedding is mandatory.
- [ ] Plan maps each implementation step to existing child beads and related 3q5/c50/pml work without duplicate ownership.
- [ ] Two adversarial review lanes plus consolidation complete with no unresolved critical finding.
- [ ] No production code changes land in this task.

## Related Work
`magic-context-c50.6`, `magic-context-c50.8`, `magic-context-3q5.25`, `magic-context-3q5.26`, `magic-context-3q5.27`, `magic-context-pml.4`.
notes: Deep research completed 2026-08-23. Committed at docs/research/embedding-model-selection-2026-08-23/ (entry point deep-research-results.md; plan phase3-plan.md; synthesis phase2-synthesis.md). Result: no model winner can be named before the in-domain campaign; evidence supports one Linux NVIDIA CUDA ONNX Runtime Synapse profile, separate execution/semantic identity by default, and exact recipe-aware evaluation. The plan now carries an architecture-open comparison benchmark specification: the incumbent pipeline is a baseline arm, FTS5 porter unicode61 plus bm25, fixed 0.7/0.3 fusion, source boosts, candidate depth, and the missing reranker are treatments under test, with 9 factors, 22 first-round arms, mandatory lexical-only and dense-only ablations, and latency, index cost, and footprint as separate gates. Critical gap remains independent in-domain candidate results and a stable judged population.

title: Extend Synapse certification for one GPU runtime profile
description:
## Context
Synapse currently certifies one CPU-only FastEmbed bundle and one hash-pinned dynamic ORT library. GPU execution adds an execution provider, provider dependencies, device requirements, and potentially a different model. Readiness must continue to mean that every byte and semantic choice is proven before requests are admitted.

## Current State
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/bundle.rs:167-229` confines and hashes every listed model/tokenizer artifact before construction.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:56-115` verifies one ORT library and commits its process-global identity.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs:129-191` constructs and structurally/semantically certifies the CPU backend.
- `docs/synapse-model-bundle.md` documents exact CPU-only artifact and feature-graph requirements.

## Desired State
Extend the existing bundle/runtime contract with the minimum fields required by the forged plan to certify one GPU execution profile. Certification must bind model bytes, tokenizer behavior, output/pooling/truncation, execution provider, native runtime and provider dependencies, target/driver compatibility, and expected resource policy.

Requests and route identity must not select any path, device, model, or provider. Expected GPU artifact or compatibility failures either select the documented CPU startup path or disable Synapse according to startup policy. Magic Context remains routable.

## Implementation Guidance
### Files to Modify
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/bundle.rs`: extend strict manifest validation only where the plan requires it.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/inference.rs`: extend committed runtime identity and pre-construction verification.
- `crates/mc-host/src/synapse/mod.rs`: extend trusted startup configuration, not request schemas.

## Acceptance Criteria
